A split system can freeze up at any stage of its life: right after installation or during operation. With special equipment, the situation can be diagnosed by measuring the refrigerant pressure:

  1. If the pressure is below normal, the cause of the freon leak must be found and the air conditioner repaired and charged;
  2. If the pressure is above normal, the cause may be excess refrigerant from doing this work yourself. Specialists must fully release the freon, evacuate the system and charge the air conditioner with the required amount of refrigerant by weight.

Freezing can also come from a lack of cleaning or proper care: dust fills the filters, fan impellers and the heat exchanger of the indoor unit. Outdoor unit faults also lead to icing, with the compressor relay on the control board or the freeze sensor on the evaporator failing. Another common mistake is trying to use the split system for heating when the outdoor temperature is low.

Indoor unit freezing up

The indoor unit can freeze up for these most common reasons:

  • Using the air conditioner in the cold season. Some split systems cannot run at sub-zero temperatures. This applies especially to heating mode.
  • Furniture placed too close to the air conditioner, creating barriers and interfering with normal air circulation. Moving furniture at least three meters away from the unit can solve the problem.
  • Compressor overload caused by failed evaporator freeze sensors or the board.
  • Dirt on parts such as the filters, evaporator and fan impellers.
  • Too little refrigerant. This can be fixed by recharging.
  • A blocked capillary tube. A special high-pressure compressor is needed to clear it.
  • A kink or poor flare in the thin copper pipe. To solve the problem, replace the whole pipe or the damaged section.

Outdoor unit freezing up

The outdoor unit can freeze up for these most common reasons:

  • Running in heating mode when the outdoor temperature is below 5 degrees Celsius.
  • Moisture getting into the unit. The thin pipe gets covered in frost or ice and freezes before everything else. Refrigerant movement becomes difficult and the whole outdoor unit freezes.
  • Too much refrigerant. Normal operation at lower temperatures is possible with less refrigerant. To stop the freezing, some freon must be removed.
  • Dirty parts: most often the heat exchanger freezes because it is contaminated with dust particles. Normal operation will be possible after cleaning.

f7c2cd80fb3809ad: There are more and more air conditioners, and their functions keep expanding. But as climate equipment improves, its design becomes more complex and there are more new parts that periodically fail. So repairing air conditioners is getting harder, from identifying the faulty unit to finding spare parts. Our service center technicians regularly train at centers opened by leading manufacturers. Manufacturers equip modern split systems with effective self-diagnostics. When a dangerous fault or malfunction is detected, they stop the equipment and show an error code on the screen. Deciphering it explains why the air conditioner is not working. If there is no display, the code is shown as a combination of light signals: indicators light up, go out and flash on the remote or the front panel of the indoor module. Faults are determined by the controller from the internal sensors, without taking external signs into account, so diagnostics do not always give an exact result. By looking at both the data in the error code and the external signs, our technicians always find the failed unit and can usually even identify the specific broken part.

What to do if an air conditioner doesn't work

Before calling a technician or trying to find the fault yourself, make sure the problem really is in the equipment and not some external factor. Check:

  1. that there is power in the network (connect an appliance that definitely works);
  2. that the split system's mode and the required room temperature are set correctly;
  3. the condition of the filters (if needed, open the cover, take the filters out of the indoor module and wash them in water that is not hot);
  4. that the drain is clear.

Most users first look at the state of the room unit: how well it works in different modes and what has changed since the fault appeared.

Sometimes the split system starts and the fan blows, but the room does not cool. In that case, make sure the motor is running. This is usually confirmed by a hum and slight vibration you can feel from the outdoor module. If the motor runs almost non-stop (the thermal protection may switch it off), the problem is most likely too little refrigerant in the circuit. To find the leak, seal the circuit and charge it with freon, you need the help of a service center. You are unlikely to have the skills, consumables and equipment for a full, quality repair.

When a compressor fails, the causes can vary, and it is impossible to say exactly what happened without thorough diagnostics. This problem is most often caused by one of these faults:

  • the motor-compressor's start capacitor has lost capacity, broken or dried out;
  • the contacts on the motor's power terminals have oxidized or burnt out;
  • thermal sensors have broken or their parameters have drifted;
  • the controller has failed or malfunctioned;
  • the electric motor or mechanical parts of the motor-compressor have broken.

An air conditioner leaks because of drainage problems (a displaced or damaged tube, a blockage, a fault in the condensate collection system) or a fault that causes ice on the evaporator (too little refrigerant, dirt on the evaporator surface, blocked capillaries and so on).

The main faults that stop an air conditioner from switching on usually lie in the IR receiver or the control panel of the indoor module. To check this, press the power button on its panel. If there is power in the network but the split system still will not start, the problem in most cases is a failed electronic controller.

Often the whole climate unit stops working properly. The air conditioner switches on and runs normally, but after a while cooling stops. The compressor will not start for a long time, and when it finally does, the hum soon stops and no more cold air comes out. In this situation, call a technician to charge the refrigerant. Do this as soon as possible, because long continuous running of the motor-compressor shortens the life of both the unit and the whole system.

How to identify a compressor failure

Signs of a burnt-out compressor may include gradually growing noise and oil streaks on its housing. The most common faults are worn shaft seals and gaskets, cracks in the housing, contamination of the circuit and failures in the motor-compressor's electrical circuits. As a rule, the faulty unit is not repaired but replaced with a new one of the same capacity.

The air conditioner's outdoor unit has stopped working

The outdoor module has several important units, including the motor-compressor. So if the outdoor unit cannot be switched on, there will be no cooling and the indoor fan will just blow warm air. The compressor motor in the outdoor module may not start for these reasons:

  1. the condenser plates are very dirty, so the unit overheats;
  2. there is too much refrigerant in the circuit;
  3. the fan does not work;
  4. a blockage has formed in the capillaries;
  5. there is moisture and dirt in the filter drier;
  6. the compressor itself has broken.

To repair the outdoor module, call service center technicians, because even a simple operation such as cleaning the condenser surface must be done with special equipment (a pressure washer or steam generator).

There are different views, but it is clear that equipment should be written off for faults that cannot be fixed or when repair would cost more than new equivalent equipment. Air conditioner error codes can differ by model and manufacturer. For the exact codes for your model, please check the service manual or the instructions that came with your air conditioner.

For example, LG error codes include 47, which means a fault in the compressor discharge sensor. Gree error codes include E3, which means a fault in the indoor unit temperature sensor. Midea error codes include 00-0C, which means a fault in the outdoor unit temperature sensor.

Let's look at the most popular air conditioner models and their errors:

Home air conditioners are complex devices that can suffer many kinds of faults for many reasons. To avoid unpleasant situations, owners need to know the main faults that can occur. For example, a dirty filter, which can disrupt air circulation and the refrigeration equipment, and cause ice on the copper pipes and excess water in the casing. To avoid such problems, wash the filters every three weeks or order regular cleaning for additional disinfection.

Another common cause of breakdowns is a freon leak. This is normal at a rate of 2-3% a year. But if the leak exceeds this, it can lead to serious problems such as mechanical faults. To avoid this, have a freon recharge regularly.

Another cause of breakdowns is running air conditioners in winter. Most units are not adapted to cold weather, which can disrupt the compressor and drainage systems. As a result, fluid leaks into the room and other faults occur.

If you have a problem with your air conditioner, it is not advisable to repair it yourself. This can void the manufacturer's warranty.


If cooling in the room is poor, the cause may be too little capacity or internal faults. In that case, it is also advisable to have it serviced.

If the air conditioner runs for only 15-20 minutes, the cause may be a dirty radiator, a failed thermostat, a broken control board or a settings error. In that case, wash the radiator and check the settings.

If condensate leaks from the indoor unit, the cause may be a blocked condensate tube. To fix this, switch off the air conditioner, wait 10 minutes, disconnect the plastic drain tube, clean and dry it, and put everything back as it was.

To avoid breakdowns, have air conditioning systems diagnosed once a year. The system is checked for leaks, and its performance and electrics are examined. After diagnostics, the air conditioner can be charged, with moisture and air fully removed.

Finally, remember that clogged indoor unit filters can cause poor cooling and drain leaks. Washing the unit's outer filter is essential.

If messages appear on the display and lights flash, this may signal a problem. Look up the most common error codes for your air conditioner. In that case, contact professionals for diagnostics and repair.

  • The chilled water temperature is above the setpoint;

1. Gathering information

Before the inspection, the circumstances of the fault are recorded:

  • When the problem appeared and in which operating mode;
  • Which alarm messages are displayed;
  • Whether settings or the system's makeup changed recently;
  • Whether repairs, recharging or service were carried out;
  • The temperature and load of the circuit being served;
  • Whether the fault is constant or intermittent.

It is useful to write down the parameters before resetting the alarm. Simply switching off and on again may clear the message for a while but will not remove its cause.

2. External inspection

The casing, pipework, electrical connections and accessible parts of the equipment are checked. The specialist looks for signs of leaks, corrosion, overheating, damaged insulation and unusual ice. On an air-cooled chiller, the heat exchanger and the area around the fans are inspected: dirt, leaves and obstructions can impair heat removal. On a water-cooled model, the accessible parts of the condenser circuit are checked. Safety rules must be followed before the inspection. Do not remove protective panels or touch electrical parts with the power on unless the procedure allows it.

3. Checking the water circuit

Insufficient water flow is one of the most common causes of reduced capacity and emergency shutdowns. The specialist checks:

  • The circulation pump;
  • Temperature and pressure sensor readings;
  • The condition of filters and mesh strainers;
  • The position of shut-off and control valves;
  • Air in the system;
  • The cleanliness of the heat exchanger;
  • Whether the flow meets the manufacturer's requirements.

The inlet and outlet water temperatures are compared with the unit's operating parameters. Deviations are assessed against the actual load and operating mode: a single value without context does not always indicate a fault.

4. Checking the air or condenser circuit

On an air-cooled chiller, the cleanliness of the heat exchanger fins, the fans and the free movement of air are assessed. The air intake and discharge areas are checked for blockages. On a water-cooled chiller, the condenser water circuit is checked, including flow, water temperature and the condition of the heat exchanger. Dirt or insufficient flow can raise the condensing pressure and stop the equipment.

5. Checking automation and sensors

The controller displays operating parameters and alarm codes, but a code does not always point to the root cause. Settings, sensor signals, protections and communication errors are checked. If in doubt, a sensor reading is compared with an independent measurement using a suitable instrument.

6. Checking the compressor and refrigerant circuit

The compressor's start and operation, its noise and vibration, and the accessible operating parameters given in the service documentation are assessed. If necessary, the specialist checks the refrigerant circuit for leaks and analyzes its condition with professional instruments. Never release refrigerant, open a sealed circuit or recharge on your own without finding the cause of the fault. A shortage of refrigerant may come from a leak, and recharging without repair can lead to losing the refrigerant again and damaging the equipment.

Regular service reduces the likelihood of unplanned shutdowns. Scheduled work includes cleaning heat exchangers, checking filters, the water circuit, pumps and fans, and monitoring sensors and automation. The service interval is set by the manufacturer's instructions and the operating conditions. Chiller diagnostics should be done before a minor deviation leads to an emergency shutdown.

It is a device that moves heat from the outdoor air into a heat transfer fluid: the water circulating in the heating and hot water system. It works on the same principle as an ordinary refrigerator, only "in reverse": it takes heat from outside and delivers it into the house.

The key advantage is that for every kilowatt of electricity used, the system can deliver 3 to 4 kW of heat to the circuit. This coefficient of performance (COP) is what saves money compared with direct electric heating.

Other advantages:

  • One unit covers heating, hot water and, if needed, cooling or pool heating.
  • No open flame, no chimney, no fuel storage.
  • No gas mains, gas service approvals or regular deliveries.
  • With correct installation, the equipment lasts 15 to 20 years or more.

9fd2d0a951bdcbc6:
A heat pump is neither an air conditioner nor an electric boiler. Installation mistakes almost always lead to lower capacity, higher electricity use, frequent automation errors and early compressor failure.

Common installation mistakes:

  • A wrongly sized buffer tank, no hydraulic separation or piping errors cause the compressor to switch on too often.
  • Heating units must be designed for low-temperature operation.
  • No dedicated power line, correct circuit breaker, grounding or voltage stabilization.
  • Condensate and meltwater must be drained so that no ice forms under the outdoor unit in winter.

That is why installation starts not with buying equipment but with a thermal engineering calculation of the site.

A fairly common problem with air conditioners is an unpleasant smell when they are switched on. This can happen for many reasons.

One common cause is microorganisms settling in the indoor unit. A split system cools by drawing in room air, which, as we know, contains small dust particles that settle inside the equipment. When warm air touches the heat exchanger, condensate forms on its surface and collects in the tray. Dust and moisture together are an excellent environment for fungal spores, which are found on the building's walls.

Air circulation then carries these microorganisms from the indoor unit into the room. They bring with them the bad smell of damp that comes with their activity. This can have a negative effect on people with various allergies and asthma.

An unpleasant smell also comes from wrongly installed drain tubes (with bends). Condensate collects in the bend, and the room fills with the smell of mold.

A drain tube going into a sewer system must have a trap. The water seal formed in its cup stops air coming back from the pipe into the room. To remove the smell effectively, the equipment must be cleaned of dust and disinfected every year, which is best left to specialists. A split system should be disinfected before its season of heavy use. The causes of an unpleasant smell may be:

  • The equipment being unused for a long time, for example when the air conditioner is only switched on in summer. To reduce the risk of odors, it must be switched on from time to time.
  • Lack of care of the climate equipment. Room air should always be clean and fresh, so the air conditioner must be disassembled, cleaned and washed on time. This work is laborious, but it is the only way to get the desired result.
  • Bad smells may also come from filters not being replaced on time, so filters should be changed regularly.

Climate Center installs, repairs and services multi-zone air conditioning systems (VRV/VRF systems).

Comfort in summer can be guaranteed with special air conditioning systems. For large buildings, the best choices are VRF systems or chillers, valued for their capacity, reliability and durability. Each of these systems has its own advantages that deserve attention.
f5f33eaa0ddd654b:
In design, VRF systems are closer to multi-system air conditioners, with one outdoor compressor unit and many indoor units. This keeps the building's facade free of many outdoor units, which also give off a lot of heat: on upper floors, the efficiency of wall-mounted versions can fall drastically because of this heat effect. VRF systems are the way out, with one unit throttling freon for many indoor units. Another advantage is that they can handle large height differences, often between 15 and 70 meters. For relatively small buildings, VRF systems are clearly the best solution: they are relatively inexpensive and provide cooling at a reasonable price.

Multi-zone air conditioning is a higher level of development of multi-split systems:

  1. the unit is part of a smart system for creating a comfortable indoor climate;
  2. the system has central control;
  3. self-diagnostics identifies faults and shuts the system down in an emergency;
  4. indoor units are usually connected to one (or several) outdoor units through a common freon line, typically of no more than 3 pipes;
  5. the lines of a multi-zone system use R410A and equivalents, which are environmentally friendly refrigerants;
  6. indoor units of different designs can be used: ducted, wall-mounted, cassette.

When installing VRV / VRF systems, the following must be taken into account:

  • the maximum permitted line length;
  • height differences between indoor and outdoor units;
  • surveying and recommending the best location for outdoor units: on the roof, in the basement or even on a neighboring building tens of meters away;
  • installing alternative ways of regulating the indoor temperature to suit the client: central control or separate control for each room by remote;
  • being able to adjust the amount of refrigerant from the common line to each indoor consumer according to the set heat load;
  • examining whether the existing line can be extended to connect a new consumer.

Using special software, our specialists will commission and set up the outdoor units of a multi-zone system for the task at hand.

With the software suite and the system's self-diagnostics, we quickly find climate control faults, which greatly reduces the time needed to repair VRV / VRF systems.
